findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion covering the 'interim evidence-run insurance' child (or fold it explicitly under an existing AC) so every described child has a covering criterion.
evidence: Approach: 'Interim evidence-run insurance — single-criterion evidence-run survival hardening that ships only while the fan-out it patches still exists.'
The five ACs map to: banked (AC1,AC2), ceilings (AC3), damping (AC4), pre-loading (AC5) — none covers the interim evidence-run insurance child.
findings.finding: The Approach section names five children including 'Interim evidence-run insurance' (single-criterion evidence-run survival hardening), but only four of the five children have covering acceptance criteria; the interim evidence-run insurance child has no AC.
findings.location: Approach section (5th bullet) vs Acceptance Criteria (5 items)
scenarios: Executor delivers the four covered children and closes the epic; the interim insurance child's completion is unverifiable against any criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC such as: 'Single-criterion evidence runs survive [specific failure] and produce a verdict; delivered by the interim evidence-run insurance child, checked by its unit suite; removed when the fan-out it patches is gone.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to 2948's scope the explicit rework/removal of 8eb3's interim _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS (context*criteria) economic bound, replacing the per-criterion multiplier with the successor_batches formula.
evidence: 8eb3 description: 'This ceiling is EXPLICITLY INTERIM: it models the per-criterion fan-out that the banked-verification sibling (2948) deletes; that sibling replaces the multiplier with successor_batches (ceil(remainder/batch_cap)), shrinking the product by ~8x.'

2948 Scope (completion_recovery.py): 'delete the per-criterion fan-out; criterion IDs; successor batching + budget pool; finalizer full-coverage + deterministic fallback; reworked coverage validation' — no mention of _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS or the economic/product bound.
2948 ACs list a request-denominated budget POOL (N=240/pool=360/successor=120) but no re-expression of the context*criteria economic char ceiling.
container pairing: parent + 2948-48e5-666f-4677/8eb3-1f20-f395-4ea5/a9dd-bbc7-f549-4fc2/ed6d-5448-4ff6-4b8a/f6fc-27fe-d3af-4f87
findings.finding: child 8eb3 introduces the economic ceiling _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS = 3_200_000 refusing when len(context) * len(criteria) exceeds it, and declares it EXPLICITLY INTERIM — modeling the per-criterion fan-out that 2948 deletes, to be replaced by successor_batches. But sibling 2948's Scope for completion_recovery.py enumerates 'delete the per-criterion fan-out; criterion IDs; successor batching + budget pool; finalizer full-coverage + deterministic fallback; reworked coverage validation' and does NOT name reworking or removing the economic ceiling / the context*criteria product bound in _validate_recovery_inputs. After 2948 deletes the fan-out, the context*criteria economic bound models a cost model that no longer exists (per-criterion re-send), yet no child owns replacing it with the successor_batches formula 8eb3 promises.
scenarios: 2948 lands after 8eb3 but leaves _validate_recovery_inputs's context*criteria product bound in place: recovery now re-sends context per BATCH (<=3 runs), not per criterion, so a stale bound sized for 32x per-criterion re-sends is both wrong and unmaintained.
A large-but-few-criteria ticket is refused (or admitted) by a bound that models a deleted cost path.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 2948's completion_recovery.py scope line to name 'replace the interim context*criteria economic ceiling with a successor_batches-denominated bound' and add a corresponding acceptance criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in a9dd whether the successor prefetch section counts toward 8eb3's context*criteria economic ceiling and 2948's per-successor re-send/pool accounting, and reconcile the three children's 'context' definition.
evidence: a9dd: 'The same prefetch section feeds recovery successor runs' and 'the 30k-token aggregate cap mirroring completion_recovery's _MAX_* pattern'.
8eb3: economic ceiling refuses when 'len(context) * len(criteria) exceeds' _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS — measured over the recovery context.

2948: successor 'FULL ticket context unchanged (no elision) ... the re-paid context cost is accepted and mitigated by the cache note' — pool arithmetic (N=240/360/120) computed on pre-prefetch context sizes.
container pairing: parent + 2948-48e5-666f-4677/8eb3-1f20-f395-4ea5/a9dd-bbc7-f549-4fc2/ed6d-5448-4ff6-4b8a/f6fc-27fe-d3af-4f87
findings.finding: child a9dd appends a bounded prefetch section (up to a 30,000-token aggregate cap) to the verifier context AND states 'The same prefetch section feeds recovery successor runs' — but does not reconcile the added prefetch volume with sibling 8eb3's economic ceiling on _validate_recovery_inputs (which refuses on len(context) * len(criteria)) nor with 2948's per-successor context re-send accounting and request-budget pool. It is unspecified whether prefetch chars enter the 'context' measured by the recovery preflight bound or the re-paid context cost that sizes 2948's pool; the three children disagree implicitly on what 'context' the successor run carries.
scenarios: a9dd ships last and enlarges the successor context by ~60k+ chars of prefetch: if that counts toward 8eb3's context*criteria product, previously-admitted shapes now refuse at preflight; if it does not count, the preflight under-measures actual re-sent bytes.
2948's per-batch request pool was sized assuming no prefetch; adding prefetch to every successor changes the re-send cost the pool was reasoned against.
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly that the prefetch section is excluded from _validate_recovery_inputs's measured context (or included with the bound adjusted), and note the prefetch's effect on 2948's successor re-send cost so the pool arithmetic accounts for it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update that captures the shared agent-call-seam memoization contract and the two-ceiling context model, so the cross-component decision is discoverable.
evidence: 'memoize duplicate read-only tool calls at the shared agent-call seam ... the shipped distinct-ratio runaway actuator stays as the abort backstop'
'replace the flat recovery char bound with a physical ceiling derived from the resolved verifier model's own context window plus an economic ceiling'
The memo changes behavior for EVERY agentic workflow, not just completion — a cross-component effect at a shared seam with no documentation artifact named.
findings.finding: The rework introduces new cross-component coupling at the shared agent_call.py tool-wrapping seam (duplicate-call memoization now affects every tool-bearing run) and a novel two-ceiling context-management design (physical model-window ceiling + economic re-send ceiling), but no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update is named to capture these architectural decisions.
findings.location: Approach — 'Duplicate-call damping ... at the shared agent-call seam' and 'Context ceilings ... two-ceiling bound'
scenarios: A future maintainer of another tool-bearing workflow sees memoized/nudged tool calls with no design doc explaining the seam-level contract, and cannot tell whether memoization is safe for non-read-only tools.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the economic ceiling's unit and a default value (or its derivation basis) at the epic level, or explicitly delegate it to the ceilings child with a stated derivation protocol.
evidence: 'an economic ceiling bounding total re-send spend' — no value, unit, or derivation stated
'under a budget clamp' — clamp value unstated
AC3: 'under the two-ceiling bound' names both ceilings but gives no economic threshold
findings.finding: The 'economic ceiling bounding total re-send spend' and the pre-loading 'budget clamp' are referenced as design elements but their concrete values/units are not stated at the epic level, and AC3's 'two-ceiling bound' does not state the second (economic) threshold.
scenarios: The ceilings child executor must decide the economic ceiling magnitude/unit (dollars? request count? total chars?) without a stated default.
findings.suggested_fix: Note that the economic ceiling and its unit are defined in the context-ceilings child, and state the derivation basis (e.g. 'bounded as N x per-run token cost against the resolved model's price') so it is not an arbitrary executor choice.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State what the mechanism produces when a primary run dies with ZERO criteria banked (e.g. the batched successor runs re-attempt the full criterion set under the budget pool, and the deterministic no-LLM fallback still emits a full-coverage verdict marking unverified criteria as such), so the verdict-less-on-zero-progress case cannot fall through to --force-close.
evidence: Plan: 'finalize to a full-coverage verdict whenever any progress is banked, with a deterministic no-LLM fallback so a run with banked progress can never die verdict-less' -- 'with banked progress' scopes the guarantee away from the zero-progress case
Plan Context: 'one live run repeated an identical search_files call 144x' and 'request-budget exhaustion that dies verdict-less' -- both can occur before the first criterion is banked
completion_recovery.py:512-545 shows verdicts accrue incrementally per criterion, so a primary run aborted early via RunawayToolLoopError (agent_call.py:106) can reach recovery with an empty bank
findings.finding: The banked-verification guarantee is scoped to runs with 'at least one criterion verdict banked', but the plan's own problem statement identifies the dominant failure as a run that exhausts or loops before any criterion completes (the 144x duplicate-call loop, request-budget exhaustion). A run that dies with ZERO banked verdicts is not covered by the full-coverage-verdict promise, so it can still die verdict-less into the --force-close trap the plan set out to close.
findings.location: Approach -> 'Banked, batched verification'; AC line 'A completion verification whose primary run dies... with at least one criterion verdict banked ends in a full-coverage verdict'
scenarios: Runaway loop trips on the first criterion; nothing is banked; batched successor runs also trip or exhaust the budget pool
c9f7-shape run whose primary dies at preflight/token-exhaustion before completing any criterion
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the banked-verification child so the deterministic no-LLM fallback fires on ANY terminal exhaustion (including zero banked verdicts), emitting a full-coverage verdict that scores every unverified criterion as unmet/undetermined rather than raising verdict-less; make the headline AC assert the zero-banked case explicitly.
